verification_report.summary:
The complete chapter passes under the specified standard inputs. Sixteen sequential records check 68 individual deductions, and five reference records verify the cited definitions, theorems and accepted prior results. No critical error or gap was found.

Analytic calculus and restriction: the rational-coefficient, bounded-remainder convention agrees with SGPT Definition 1.6.1. Common rational coefficients, powers and products of generator families, and the elementary maximum inequality prove the three closure properties. A nonzero coherent image ideal on connected Y has a proper zero set, so restricting the bounded-remainder inequalities gives a genuine quasi-psh restriction of the asserted type. Smoothness of the remainder is not assumed. [SGPT, Section 1.6](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT.pdf).

Local Bergman estimates: point evaluation, submean and point extension give both bounds with constants independent of m. The convergence argument also works at poles; the bounds give local L1 convergence. Dividing by log r^2 reverses the inequalities and contributes exactly -n/m. The substitution psi=2phi identifies the weights and preserves the normalized Lelong numbers. The real-parameter sentence correctly extends the construction and numerical estimates; subsequent rational analytic-type assertions use integer m.

Global input: the supplied July 2011 Demailly text, Theorem 14.12, pp.142-143, explicitly permits an arbitrary continuous lower bound gamma on a compact complex manifold. Proposition 5.7 and (14.7)-(14.8) identify the local generators with I_source(m(phi-q_j))=I_source(mphi). The corrections after Lemma 14.11 are smooth. The glued logarithm on p.142 is comparable to each active local Bergman norm by Lemma 14.10 and a cutoff equal to one. Thus the construction supplies ordinary type (1/(2m),I_source(mphi)); setting u=2phi gives exactly (1/m,I(mu)). This ideal identification follows from the construction, beyond the theorem's abbreviated wording. The same substitution yields all the claimed convergence, curvature and Lelong properties. Applying it to the closed current ddc u with gamma=-theta is valid even when theta is nonclosed. [Demailly, July 2011 source](/Users/mingchen/Non-Kahler/research/sources/Demailly-analytic-methods.txt:8170).

Uniform bounds: the previously verified Gauduchon trace identity bounds the positive linear trace independently of v. The fixed local quadratic correction makes ddc(v+r) closed and positive, allowing the accepted local mass-Lelong estimate. Metric comparison and a finite nested cover make the bound uniform over every center without normalizing v.

Restricted divisorial bounds: m nu(u,y)<1 gives I(mu)_y=O by Skoda in the stated normalization. Each restricted analytic ideal is therefore nonzero, and the restriction and modification pullback are genuine. Their curvature inequalities place all pullbacks in PSH(Z,C h) for one fixed Hermitian background. The uniform Lelong lemma then bounds every generic divisorial order independently of m. No bounded Monge-Ampere mass assumption, mass convergence, or earlier PDE re-audit is used.
